title: Scenario runner: an external driver contract (--driver external:<cmd>) and a Codex driver, so the same card can measure other agent tools; check WorkBuddy
body:
epic:#3600#1 · hotlong · session_01Q4EjjPXwX1YfHyKJUh4agu

Filing-gate category: ② maintainer-directed task. Maintainer, verbatim (Claude Code session, 2026-11-07), after asking 「你的画廊测试我可以用 workbuddy 或者 codex 测试吗？有没有入口？」, 「你现在本地测试画廊，用的什么模型」 and 「我用 Claude code 云任务可以测试画廊吗？」, then answering the seat's proposals: 「前面的建议都同意，立卡」. Routing, verbatim: 「能交给车队开发的你不要自己开发」. Epic: objectstack-ai/cloud#3600. Live runs are paused by the maintainer (cloud#3600, 2026-11-07), so verify with the recorded driver and unit tests; no live run is owed.

## Problem

`run-scenarios` drives only the local Claude Code CLI (`--driver claude`) or a replay (`--driver recorded:F`) (`packages/qa/scenarios/src/runner/cli.ts`, `makeDriver`). So the same card cannot measure another agent tool (OpenAI Codex CLI, Tencent WorkBuddy, …). Yet a side-by-side comparison of agent tools on the same verified card is exactly what the gallery can show.

## Ask

1. **An external driver contract.** Document the `AgentDriver` seam (`driver.ts`: `author(task)` builds in a project directory with shell and file tools; `ask(task)` answers one persona turn over the app's MCP with that persona's API key and returns a `ParsedTurn`: reply text, tool calls and outputs, meta) as a process contract. An external command gets the task on stdin as JSON and prints the turn as JSON. Add `--driver external:<command>`. Keys go in a 0600 file, never on argv, as the Claude driver does.
2. **A Codex driver** (`--driver codex`) on that contract, using the Codex CLI's non-interactive mode with JSON output and its MCP configuration for `ask` turns. Measure the real flags on the installed CLI; do not assume them. Refuse an API-key login the same way the Claude driver does, unless the maintainer rules otherwise.
3. **WorkBuddy:** check whether it has a headless mode with structured output and MCP client support. If it does, wire it through the external contract. If not, say so in the PR; do not build a UI bridge.
4. The run record and the scorecard name the driver and its version (already done for Claude). The gallery exporter (#30349) shows the driver on each app page.

Reader: the `domain:devx` lane seat, from `pm:queue`.
